title: Repeat Cancellations on an Event Services Agreement
content:
A Private Event & Banquet Services diary that has already lost events to cancellation is read as well, over the twelve months ending on the day the charge is raised.

## The repeat percentage

1. Where the agreement has already carried two or more cancellation charges in those twelve months, the repeat percentage is the higher repeat uplift, being 10 per cent.
2. Where the agreement has carried exactly one cancellation charge in those twelve months, the repeat percentage is the lower repeat uplift, being 5 per cent.
3. Where the agreement has carried no cancellation charge in those twelve months, there is no repeat percentage.

The cancellation charges counted are those already raised on the same event services agreement, whatever booking they answered, and the twelve months are counted back from the day the charge now in hand is raised.

## Where the repeat percentage stands

The percentage the charge is worked at is the notice percentage and the repeat percentage added together and held to one hundred, and the charge is that percentage of the contracted event value standing in the cancellation entry.

| Cancellation charges on the agreement in the twelve months | Repeat percentage |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | None |
| 1 | 5 per cent |
| 2 | 10 per cent |
| 3 or more | 10 per cent |

## Worked illustrations on hypothetical records

An agreement carrying one earlier cancellation charge inside the twelve months, on a booking whose notice percentage is 60 per cent, is worked at 60 and 5 together, that is 65 per cent of the contracted event value standing in the cancellation entry.

An agreement carrying four earlier cancellation charges inside the twelve months, on a booking whose notice percentage is 95 per cent, is worked at 95 and 10 together, which is held to one hundred, so the charge is 100 per cent of that value.
